target_customer: Individuals and couples who pay for on-demand relationship and dating coaching
problem: People struggle with dating and relationship problems and cannot reach a trusted expert quickly. Relationship Hero connects them to coaches by chat, phone or video.
business_model: Consumer pay-per-session or subscription coaching marketplace

founders.name: Liron Shapira
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO and host of DoomDebates.com. A podcast summary names Lior Gotesman as co-founder, but no company or YC source was opened to confirm, so he is not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and session-booking app with chat, phone and video. The hard part is acquiring customers and coaches, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Easy to copy as a product, but organic search and content traffic can be a durable advantage, per a First MRR mention of organic growth.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found. Later competitors listed by review sites include Lasting and OurRitual, undated to the batch.

market_need_then: Dating and relationship advice was a large consumer topic, but no dated 2017 spend or demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses the exact relationshiphero.com domain per the YC page.
branding.community_and_virality: Hundreds of consumer reviews on Trustpilot and review sites, plus a Product Hunt listing.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and memorable name in a consumer category with many third-party reviews, but no source ties growth to the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Relationship Hero raised little outside capital, about $2M seed per aggregators, yet reached a listed team of 100 and single-digit millions of annual revenue per a First MRR case study. It appears to have grown through organic acquisition and remains active, so it looks like a capital-efficient consumer services company.
notes: Funding seen only on aggregators and with conflicting dates: a $2M seed dated 2017-12 by Startupintros and 2018-11 by CB Insights and Seedtable, with Foundation Capital, Village Global, Shrug Capital and Y Combinator named. Treated as unverified, so no round is recorded. CB Insights total $2.12M over 3 rounds. First MRR page revenue figures are internally inconsistent and undated. A MarketScreener profile claims a 2009 founding by other people and was discarded. No dated 2017 competitor sources were found. Completeness pass: the 2M seed rests on databases only (Seedtable and CB Insights date it 2018-11, Startupintros 2017-12), so the date is null. CB Insights shows 2.12M total over 3 rounds. A search summary calls Lior Gotesman a co-founder, but the YC page lists only Liron Shapira and no named outlet was opened, so he is not added.
